notes.title: Progress report: February 2023
notes.notes:
[b]Hello survivors,[/b]

Welcome to the monthly progress report covering the major aspects I worked on in February 2023. As always, if you do prefer bullet points and not read everything in detail you can skip the sections after the TL;DR part.

[b]TL;DR:[/b]
[list]
[*] Improved mod creation pipeline
[*] Further extended mod system
[*] Created main menu and mod selection menu
[*] Extended and implemented my own serialization system with the mod system to work around a big limitation in Unity’s serialization system when using runtime code injection via the mod system
[*] Set up basic character mod
[*] Brainstormed game logo design ideas
[/list]

Feel free to follow on any of the social media platforms or join the discord for more in depth and more frequent update posts.

[h2]New Menus[/h2]
With the course on UI Toolkit in January I felt comfortable to start the creation of the various menus. After a couple iterations due to new things I learned after the previous iterations I found a good workflow that makes it easy to create the menus and also give great modding capabilities to them as well. This means modders can fairly easily mod the visuals of an existing menu without having to worry about functionality breaking. Of course functionality could also be modded but that does require additional expertise. How all the things can be modded and what guidelines need to be followed to ensure stability is something I need to eventually take care of by writing proper documentation but that is something for the future. Thanks to the easy separation of functionality and visuals I put most of my attention on the functionality for now and take care of the visuals at a later time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41379564/4c48854f0f1f469d67878d89ad323a131c7c5d1d.gif[/img]

[h2]Mod System Improvements[/h2]
With the modding support being a very important feature to the game and me also using it to implement most systems into the game, the mod creation pipeline is very important. To not have to do certain tasks manually every time a new mod is created I spent some time this month making most of the steps automatic by clicking a few buttons. This significantly speeds up the creation and updating process for mods. While working on my mods I discovered a pretty big limitation of Unity’s serialization (how things are stored in files) system and runtime code injection. This limitation meant that a very important data container was rendered useless when mods want to inject custom code into the game that relies on such a container. After a lot of testing I did manage to find a suitable workaround for this by using my own custom serialization system I built in the past. I had to build this system for my modular spawning system due to another Unity serialization limitation. I probably would not have attempted to create one from scratch if I didn’t have this one already available because it was unclear if this would even help resolve this issue. Fortunately it worked pretty well and while it’s not a perfect solution it is a solution third party mods should not have any issue working with. After building the mod selection menu I noticed that some additional criterias/settings for a mod are required. For that I now added a mod config file that mods use to specify the version, an image/avatar and a custom display name. There is probably going to be more added to the config in the future as I find more settings to be required for either functionality or convenience.

[h2]Setup Basic Character Mod[/h2]
The asset that I used for the creation of the character recently received a massive update. For that I decided to start creating the character using that asset from scratch to make use of all the new functionalities and get familiar with it. Much of the old character I will take for reference in order to get the new character on par soon. So far I’ve only created a basic character with it in order to not spend too much time on it just yet. The process went pretty smooth and it is part of its own dedicated mod now.

[h2]Miscellaneous[/h2]
The current game logo for both the art and text are placeholders. I plan to commission an artist soon to create me a proper logo and game name representation. In preparation I did some brainstorming on what I am looking for with the logo and text logo to better be able to convey my vision to the artist. 

[h2]Plans for March[/h2]
The focus for March is on the new implementation of the game starting process. This requires a handful of systems to be set up which are not in the core project yet. This includes systems like the save and load system. I don’t expect this to take too long as it mostly requires me to extract the setup from the old project or use the old project simply as reference. After that I want to create a proper new game functionality which for example will integrate the loading and initializing of the enabled mods. Once the game can technically be started the unloading and removal/recycling of aspects in the various mods needs to be implemented for the case that a user goes back to the main menu and enables a different combination of mods. Once those systems are implemented I can focus on bringing back various features. The world generation pipeline will likely be the first one to get back into the game as most of the other systems rely on it. I don’t expect to get to the world generation pipeline in March but we’ll see how fast the other system implementations will go.

I’m looking forward to reading your thoughts, feedback or criticism in the Steam discussions.

That’s it for this update post. I hope you are all doing well.
Stay safe out there and I’ll see you in the next one.

Norman aka CitrioN

notes.title: Progress report: January 2023
notes.notes:
[b]Hello survivors,[/b]

Welcome to the monthly progress report covering the major aspects I worked on in January 2023. As always, if you do prefer bullet points and not read everything in detail you can skip the sections after the TL;DR part.

[b]TL;DR:[/b]
[list]
[*] Finished setting up the new computer
[*] Took an online course on Unity’s new UI system called UI Toolkit
[*] Started codebase for new UI implementations
[*] Updated project to Unity version 2022
[*] Lots of project restructuring
[/list]

Feel free to follow on any of the social media platforms or join the discord for more in depth and more frequent update posts.

[h2]Project Management[/h2]
Most of January (likely also February) was filled with work related to getting the project organized and restructured. I wanted to do this for a while now but with the new computer and essentially a clean work environment I decided it would be the best time to do that when switching from one computer to another. Instead of simply copying over the whole project and continuing work I am actually extracting the various systems from the old project and move them into multiple separate projects. Since modding support was not planned when I originally started working on the game there is a lot of legacy stuff and things that do not use or were not built for modding support. In order to add modding support to those systems and clean up the project this step by step approach is necessary. This step ensures that project maintenance as well as extendability will not be something to worry about thanks to the nice separation of different systems into different Unity projects. Especially with large projects like this one, the ever increasing size of assets in your folders slows down the workspace a lot and I definitely felt that over the past year or so. Most of the separation is already done and the speed at which I can work and iterate on things is incredible. I’m really happy to have finally taken this step and the time invested now will definitely pay off in the long run.

[h2]UI Toolkit Adventures & UI code base[/h2]
Unity’s new UI system called UI Toolkit has been production ready for a few months now and my initial experience with it during the creation of the first world generation tech demo was great. Since it is going to be the preferred system to build menus/UI going forward I want to also take that step and build my UI with it. For that I’ve now taken an online course to make sure I definitely have all the basics covered. That course was well worth it and I think I have a pretty good understanding of how to work with it efficiently. I’ve already practiced quite a bit and also started a new codebase to integrate functionality with it. That codebase integrates nicely with my old UI system codebase thanks to an additional layer of abstraction I created when I originally created the UI codebase for my project. This now allows me to transition to the UI system without everything breaking. I can even keep some menus based on the old UI system if need be.

[h2]Upgrade to Unity version 2022[/h2]
I’ve decided to update all the projects to Unity 2022 even before the long term support for that version is ready. Usually I would want to wait for that long term support (LTS) version to come out because it guarantees the most stability but the UI Toolkit features in Unity 2021 are lacking. If I want to make the most of UI Toolkit updating to Unity 2022 is essential and since it should only be a couple more month until the LTS version comes out I decided it’s best to do it now while I create all the new projects for the game. This way I don’t have to take that additional step of upgrading all the projects in a few months again when I can skip it now by immediately creating all the new projects in Unity 2022.

[h2]New Computer[/h2]
My new computer is now fully set up and I am really enjoying the increased productivity I have working on it.

I’m looking forward to reading your thoughts, feedback or criticism in the Steam discussions.

That’s it for this update post. I hope you are all doing well.
Stay safe out there and I’ll see you in the next one.

Norman aka CitrioN

notes.title: Progress report: December 2022
notes.notes:
[b]Happy new year survivors,[/b]

Welcome to the monthly progress report covering the major aspects I worked on in December 2022. As always, if you do prefer bullet points and not read everything in detail you can skip the sections after the TL;DR part.

[b]TL;DR:[/b]
[list]
[*] Finished first implementation of new road mesh generation asset to improve road quality
[*] Added guardrail generation to roads
[*] Replaced road textures
[*] Lots of feature/task planning for 2023
[*] New computer setup and organization
[/list]

Feel free to follow on any of the social media platforms or join the discord for more in depth and more frequent update posts.

[h2]New Road Generation System[/h2]
I finished the switch from the old road mesh generation system to the new one. The intersections now work and I also managed to implement the generation of guard rails where the road angle exceeds a certain threshold. There is still quite a bit of work related to roads to be done but the core foundation is now working and in a state where I can focus on other tasks before further extending the road generation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41379564/edfec51b05cff496fe294d30d446e6a19381b3cb.png[/img]

[h2]World Generation Tech Demo v1 Benchmark Results[/h2]
I got a good amount of benchmark results from the first generation tech demo. Thanks to everyone who participated. The hardware was decently varied and I’ve not seen anything that could cause issues down the road. Performance was overall very satisfying and gives me confidence that I can stay within the performance target for the game with the feature additions I plan to make.

[h2]New Computer[/h2]
My new computer also finally arrived in December. Unfortunately it comes with a pretty annoying high pitched noise, most likely originating from the power supply unit. I wasn’t able to resolve this with the company that built and shipped the computer. However, I was able to handle it myself by getting a new cabinet and adding a bunch of acoustic foam inside. With the back of the cabinet removed, the computer inside does get more than enough air flow for cooling and thanks to the acoustic foam the noise gets reduced enough for it to not be an issue anymore. This took up quite a bit of my time in December and even now in January. With Christmas, holidays and new years happening in December I was not able to work on anything else that month. I’m currently in the process of finalizing the setup of the new computer such as installing and configuring the remaining programs and projects. I hope to continue development of the game on the new computer within the next 1 to 2 weeks.


I’m looking forward to reading your thoughts, feedback or criticism in the Steam discussions.

That’s it for this update post. I hope you are all doing well.
Stay safe out there and I’ll see you in the next one.

Norman aka CitrioN

notes.title: Progress report: November 2022
notes.notes:
[b]Hello survivors,[/b]

Welcome to the monthly progress report covering the major aspects I worked on in November 2022. As always, if you do prefer bullet points and not read everything in detail you can skip the sections after the TL;DR part.

[h2]TL;DR:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added new weather and time of day system
[*] Significantly improved the road network generation speed
[*] Created world generation v1 tech demo with automatic benchmark system
[*] Started working on algorithm for road network generation inside towns
[*] Started implementation of new road mesh generation asset to improve road quality
[/list]

Feel free to follow on any of the social media platforms or join the discord for more in depth and more frequent update posts.

[h2]Road Network Algorithm[/h2]
With the road network generation taking up the majority (80 - 90%) of the world generation time I decided to spend a good amount of time to improve the efficiency of the road network generation. I managed to increase the generation speed of roads up to 3 times the previous time. This massive improvement took down the world generation times so much that I was able to increase the maximum world size to 100km² (39~ mi²)  from previously 64km² (~ 25mi²). I also started working on the road network generation for inside towns. While I have a basic version working, it’s too early to showcase. Finally I decided to use a different asset for the road mesh generation as the current one does not support the connection of different road types and lacks support for proper intersections. I already managed to synchronize the roads with the new asset but am currently having a bit of trouble with the intersection generation and placement. I do expect to be able to resolve that and continue from there once I manage to fix it. The new road system will also come with some nice algorithms that make things like bridge generation or the automatic placements of guard rails at appropriate locations along the roads much easier.

[h2]New Weather & Time Of Day System[/h2]
I wasn’t really satisfied with the performance of the old system so I decided to give another one a try. To my surprise that integration was swift and easy. The performance was better and the quality was much better too. As this new system is much more based on features available within the high definition render pipeline I am hopeful that it might allow me to also add modding support to the weather and time of day systems which would have been much more difficult with the old systems. However, this support will not be worked on any time soon but it's always good to look ahead when it comes to integrating third party systems. Below are a few screenshots featuring the new weather and time of day system in generated worlds.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41379564/aaf4df626164de6cf79592779116c4ad045751a7.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41379564/0991039a6607c5690f222a07fbc1602aee01a8ea.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41379564/5e757d65ed80ab747ff6f077789b7957944f58a9.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41379564/bbfb063950c16a2f679fecd54dcf59d02bb5c667.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41379564/06f250f7839652c12bf24b56dc956cb72e1e9807.jpg[/img]

[h2]World Generation Tech Demo v1[/h2]
I decided to set up a very basic tech demo for the world generation to allow me to get some initial feedback and benchmarking results that allow me to better estimate the performance impact of that system on various hardware. This first, very basic tech demo is available on [url=https://ozonewipeout.itch.io/ozone-wipeout]itch[/url] and accessible by anyone who wants to try it. If you decide to give it a try be aware that there is no gameplay whatsoever as the focus is purely on the generation aspect. I didn’t even bother making convenient controls because I really didn’t want to spend more time than is necessary to get the benchmark results I need. I will be having more tech demos available as the world generation evolves but don’t expect to have any gameplay included for quite a while. Once gameplay can be included, the demos will be available here on steam.

[h2]General[/h2]
I had quite a bit of personal stuff to take care of this month so development time was unfortunately cut short once again. I also did order a new computer since my current one from 2014 is starting to show serious problems and I don’t really want to invest time into fixing a soon to be a decade old system but rather switch to a new one before the existing one completely falls apart. I’m very much looking forward to working on that new one within a few weeks.

[h2]Plans for December[/h2]
The primary goal for December is to keep working on the road mesh generation improvements and town road generation algorithm I started in November. After that I will continue with the tasks I didn’t get to work on in November such as the generation of rivers and lakes.


I’m looking forward to reading your thoughts, feedback or criticism in the Steam discussions.

That’s it for this update post. I hope you are all doing well.
Stay safe out there and I’ll see you in the next one.

Norman aka CitrioN

notes.title: Progress report: October 2022
notes.notes:
[b]Hello survivors,[/b]

Welcome to the monthly progress report covering the major aspects I worked on in October 2022. As always, if you do prefer bullet points and not read everything in detail you can skip the sections after the TL;DR part.

[h2]TL;DR:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Implemented new (finite) world generation algorithms featuring
[list]
[*] Worlds up to 64km² or ~25miles²
[*] Mountain ranges as natural world borders
[*] Mountains and hills with forests and meadows
[*] Future points of interest position evaluation
[*] Road network to connect all points of interests[/list]
[*] Implemented new vegetation renderer
[*] Used UI Toolkit (new production ready Unity UI system) to create world generation setting menu for upcoming tech demo and get experience with the new system for future UIs
[/list]

Feel free to follow on any of the social media platforms or join the discord for more in depth and more frequent update posts.


[b]Procedural world generated with new algorithms[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41379564/03967ba68e281cc9e8e4ef4ef35799b36c2fe603.jpg[/img]

[b]World overview (White circles represent points of interest connected with a road network)[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41379564/b14a6271d0badbeb635a3032f074e43ac4efae33.jpg[/img]

[h2]New World Generation Algorithms[/h2]
After additional testing of a new asset for designing worlds I decided to give it a try to reimplement the procedural world generation for the game utilizing the features of said asset. The asset is not specifically designed for my use case, meaning it’s intended use is to create worlds manually during design time. However, with some input from the asset creator I was able to make it work at runtime too. So far I was going for infinite procedural worlds but over time this turned out to make certain things incredibly difficult to implement and balance so I made the decision to take a step back and attempt to create the new world generation algorithms for a finite world. This for example allows me to ensure much easier that certain points of interest are always within a reasonable distance to the player. With the asset working at runtime I immediately started working on the new algorithms and thanks to the functionalities provided by the asset I was able to quickly make visible progress. With the rapid progress of the first week I decided to focus all my efforts in October on getting the world generation as far progressed as possible. I am happy to say that the core of the world generation is already implemented. This current implementation allows the generation of worlds up to 8x8km (64km² or ~25miles²). Those worlds have mountain ranges at the edges of the world as natural borders. Mountains and hills are also already available and can be increased or decreased in a world generation settings menu. Vegetation placement functionality is also already implemented. To not waste time on crazy variety and density I went with a basic forest and some grass land with a couple flowers for demo purposes only. Next month I will put some time into more diversity of vegetation to give the world an even better look.  As mentioned in the September progress report this change means also stepping away from my current vegetation renderer and replacing it with a new one. Fortunately this change went quick and without issues. An algorithm to evaluate viable positions/spots for future towns and other points of interest is also already in place. Those points can already be connected via a road network. This leaves only the generation of towns as part of the absolute core world generation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41379564/5796acf8c50336439c30da7ba9e8b05ba22b4460.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41379564/e7d272682d1de983f29c2ae11a7facbf3809bfc1.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41379564/0f9a7b7958249b595dc33f294fa00d33384a0494.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41379564/a2f4cd841adab88930b12a8aa953371a2412aed6.jpg[/img]

[h2]UI Toolkit - Unity’s new UI system[/h2]
With Unity’s UI Toolkit being production ready as of late I decided to familiarize myself with it. The old/current UI system in Unity is quite bad when it comes to performance and as I heard good things about the new one it was important to take a look at it before making any new UI for the game. As the upcoming world generation tech demo does require a simple UI to allow the various settings to be chosen it was the perfect time to learn and practice the workflow of UI Toolkit. The workflow is quite different but so far I am really happy with improved modularity and simplicity of the system. I did create a very basic settings menu for the world generation tech demo and will likely use this system for any future UI implementation and will also consider porting over existing UI in the game.

[h2]Plans for November[/h2]
The primary goal for November is to add support for generating the town roads and having basic building placements. With those 2 features in place, the core world generation would be complete. To add more vegetation variety I will also be taking a look at biome placement which would allow dedicated vegetation to be placed in specific areas of the world. The addition of rivers and/or lakes are also planned but I don’t know how long the implementation of the previous features will take me so it’s hard to say if I will be able to take a look at those in November.


I’m looking forward to reading your thoughts, feedback or criticism in the Steam discussions.

That’s it for this update post. I hope you are all doing well.
Stay safe out there and I’ll see you in the next one.

Norman aka CitrioN

notes.title: Progress report: September 2022
notes.notes:
[b]Hello survivors,[/b]

Welcome to the monthly progress report covering the major aspects I worked on in September 2022. As always, if you do prefer bullet points and not read everything in detail you can skip the sections after the TL;DR part.

[h2]TL;DR:[/h2]
[list]
[*] More tweaks to high definition render pipeline (HDRP) setup
[*] Researched and planned upcoming zombie implementation using UMA (Unity Multipurpose Avatar)
[*] Researched new asset to improve world generation
[*] Took about a 2 week break due to covid
[/list]

Feel free to follow on any of the social media platforms or join the discord for more in depth and more frequent update posts.

[h2]General[/h2]
I started off the month by doing more tweaks to the high definition render pipeline settings along with a lot of testing to make sure to stay within the performance requirements. There are a couple more systems left to be updated to HDRP before I can integrate them back into the game, most importantly the terrain shading. This will be worked on in October to hopefully get everything fully working as before. For that reason I am currently still using the default Unity terrain shader in the screenshots of this progress update. Unfortunately I got Covid and while I never had a fever or felt too bad I decided to take it slow and take a break from development for about 2 weeks. This means development time this month was significantly less than I planned for.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41379564/ce69ed48eaef9574b0fba15420de0d2ca84413ec.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41379564/b6fba947ba9229b9ae1c63f00dc5386c2e6e388b.jpg[/img]

[h2]Zombie Research & Planning[/h2]
Most of my time this month went into researching, testing and planning the upcoming zombie implementation. For that I explored various approaches before finally coming back to an asset called UMA. This asset is freely available and offers the necessary versatility I need to create modular zombies. During research of the asset I discovered that 7 Days To Die also makes use of that asset for their zombies which further strengthens my believe that it is possible to achieve modular zombies with modding support using UMA. The nature of it being free allows me to add modding support for zombies much easier because I don’t have to deal with licensing or copyright which would be the case for alternative approaches. The asset does come with a set of human models which I will be basing the zombies on to also make it easier for modders to add contents to the zombies like custom clothing models. Since the human models are of course not really looking like zombies I will be doing initial retexturing of the skin, applying blood platter and possibly some wound overlays in combination with custom facial expressions and of course animations to make them look and feel more like zombies. Once the zombies are implemented on a technical level and I can be sure to stick to this asset and models I will commission a professional character artist to do the necessary changes to give the zombies the quality I am looking for. Waiting for that gives me the option to still decide on whether or not I think fully custom 3D models are required and if need be commission them instead. Unfortunately due to my covid break and the required thorough planning for the zombie implementation to meet all its requirements there was not much time for anything else this month.

[h2]Plans for October[/h2]
Since the zombie implementation is a huge task I will not solely focus on it for October. Unexpectedly the creator of the terrain shader I am soon going to be implementing back into the game just released a new asset for environment creation. I already spent a bit of time looking into the asset to see if it would help me with certain tasks in my world generation pipeline. From what I can tell it should fit nicely into my pipeline and even potentially allow me to skip certain implementations I had planned for in the future. However, this integration won’t be a quick one as it would require me to step away from my current vegetation placement and rendering asset. While this may sound bad it’s actually a good thing because the current asset for that has not received any updates in a long time and may break in future Unity versions. With the uncertainty of the future of that asset I currently rely on and the absence of the developer of said asset I think it’s well worth the time to try and switch to another vegetation rendering system and utilize the new asset to manage vegetation placement. I’ve already found a potential replacement for the new vegetation rendering too and will be looking into that a bit in October. Ultimately I think this switch could prevent running into serious issues later in development and save me time in the long run by taking the step now while it’s much easier to do than later. I will be doing a good amount of tests before making any final decisions but that is certainly where some of my time in October will be allocated for.

I’m looking forward to reading your thoughts, feedback or criticism in the Steam discussions.

That’s it for this update post. I hope you are all doing well.
Stay safe out there and I’ll see you in the next one.

Norman aka CitrioN

notes.title: Progress report: August 2022
notes.notes:
[b]Hello survivors,[/b]

Welcome to the monthly progress report covering the major aspects I worked on in August 2022. As always, if you do prefer bullet points and not read everything in detail you can skip the sections after the TL;DR part.

[h2]TL;DR:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Researched and tested new high definition render pipeline (HDRP) for improved visuals
[*] Upgraded project to use the HDRP
[/list]

Feel free to follow on any of the social media platforms or join the discord for more in depth and more frequent update posts.

In the month of August I decided to switch from the builtin to the high definition render pipeline which offers significantly better visuals. With the summer break until mid August the pipeline switch took up all the remaining development time of the month so there isn't a lot to talk about in this progress report.

[h2]Switch To High Definition Render Pipeline (HDRP)[/h2]
After my summer break I wanted to continue working on the zombie implementation but didn’t get far due to some performance issues I ran into with the basic implementation. After considering my options I made the decision to go on an unplanned detour instead. This was to take the rest of the month and test out Unity’s high definition render pipeline. With the recent change to photorealistic graphics the render pipeline switch made sense especially before going forward with the zombie visuals as they will be directly impacted by the new render pipeline. It’s always better to do these kinds of switches sooner than later as they will always require conversions of existing assets. Since such a switch is no small task and I had no prior experience with the HDRP I decided to first get familiar with the pipeline before making the final decision of switching. I first started testing out a good amount of the pipeline in different projects and did some asset conversion too. Since the HDRP provides better visual quality it also comes with a bigger performance impact. To be able to get a feeling on how much that would mean in my project I also tested various scenarios in both the builtin (current) and HDRP (new) pipeline.
The switch also required me to replace the weather asset I previously used because it is not compatible with the HDRP. I quickly found an alternative weather asset I could use and after over a week of learning and testing of the pipeline I decided it’s worth going forward and actually do the switch to the new render pipeline. I managed to finish the core part of the switch just by the end of August. Unfortunately not everything is set up yet to actually showcase the new visuals in the game. I will be showcasing the visuals in the progress report of September when I had more time to tweak all the settings and get the best visuals possible without compromising performance too much. The new render pipeline comes with a whole bunch of new visual features that the builtin render pipeline doesn’t provide. I hope to be able to make use of at least a few of them in September and showcase them in the next progress report too.

I’m looking forward to reading your thoughts, feedback or criticism in the Steam discussions.

That’s it for this update post. I hope you are all doing well.
Stay safe out there and I’ll see you in the next one.

Norman aka CitrioN

[*] Extended procedural temperate forest biome generation
[*] Conducted new tech demo testing
[*] Created and integrated new navigation mesh generation into world generation pipeline
[*] UMA (Unity Multipurpose Avatar) asset research
[*] Began new AI implementation
[/list]

Feel free to follow on any of the social media platforms or join the discord for more in depth and more frequent update posts.

In the month of July I conducted another tech demo testing with a few selected testers. The tech demo focused on performance optimizations, the look and feel of the generated forest biome and the new drawer mechanics. The testing went well, I got valuable feedback and performance was better than I was expecting.

[h2]New AI implementation[/h2]
The biggest focus for the month was researching and preparing the implementation of the new zombie AI. For that I had to test a variety of available options. A major goal for the zombies is to have them very customizable and actually wearing the clothing and items that the player can scavenge from the respective zombie. This allows the player to make more logical choices to avoid or take on a zombie based on the information available. For that I did research and test a Unity asset called UMA that provides the flexibility I need. While I haven’t actively integrated the asset into the project yet the research and testing looked promising to allow me to achieve the zombie customization I need. Modding support is another big factor to take into consideration when deciding on how I want to implement AI. As UMA being a free asset it will be available to modders as well. This allows for example to easily integrate custom clothing into their mods thanks to the capabilities of UMA. After stress testing my old AI behaviour implementation I came to the conclusion that I could not go forward with it due to performance issues that would likely arise later. After more research and testing I did decide on a new approach on the implementation and already started working on the fundamentals for it. I didn’t get it to a presentable state for this progress report so there won’t be any showcasing of it yet. The existing navigation mesh handling (the most common approach to handle AI pathing) also had its performance issues due to constant rebaking causing the occasional very noticeable frame drop. With the new world generation pipeline I was able to easily refactor the code to make the navigation mesh baking based on world chunks, significantly reducing performance impact. Altogether the new implementation is going well and so far is holding up with the performance target I have set for it.

[h2]Summer Break[/h2]
I’ll be taking a 2 week break in August to get some rest. This means there won’t be as much progress in the next progress report as I will only be working on the game for about 2 weeks. 
I’ll be checking out some of the survival games taking part in the steam survival fest this week and I highly recommend checking them out yourself too.

I’m looking forward to reading your thoughts, feedback or criticism in the Steam discussions.

That’s it for this update post. I hope you are all doing well.
Stay safe out there and I’ll see you in the next one.

Norman aka CitrioN

notes.title: Progress report: June 2022
notes.notes:
[b]Hello survivors,[/b]

Welcome to the monthly progress report covering the major aspects I worked on in June 2022. If you do prefer bullet points and not read everything in detail you can skip the sections after the TL;DR part.
Feel free to follow on any of the social media platforms or join the discord for more in depth and more frequent update posts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41379564/6f19e1104a797e45bee22e5121844e7ac32e00c0.jpg[/img]

[h2]TL;DR:[/h2]
[list]
[*]Integrated more immersive scavenging mechanics
[*]Reworked integration for realtime procedural vegetation
[*]Added basic biome assignment/distribution to the world generation pipeline
[*]Setup temperate and boreal forest biomes
[*]Implemented new terrain shader
[*]Integrated automatic biome based terrain texturing
[/list]

[h2]Immersive scavenging[/h2]
With looting/scavenging being a major aspect of the game the goal is to make this experience as immersive as possible. I've previously tried the commonly used UI based inventory/container approach but that didn't feel very immersive due to the frequent cut between the first person view and the UI overlay. To avoid a UI approach entirely I decided to work with physical items that exist in the game instead of residing in an inventory UI represented by a simple icon. While this dramatically improves the experience, it does come with a couple challenges. More physical objects in the world mean the graphics card needs to render more objects and impacts performance. There are many optimization methods to counteract the additional rendering of those objects. Since I have already implemented many of such systems in the past it should be possible to keep the additional impact quite low. Physical items and real containers such as drawers also require more accurate collision detection and limits the type of objects that can fit into them due to the shape of the object and the container. Placing items in such containers is also more challenging since it no longer is a simple addition of the object to a list but instead needs to check for a valid position inside the physical container. All of those things combined add a whole lot of additional work to implement and manage such a system. Ultimately I do believe that the additional work and required performance optimizations are worth the experience players get when it's fully implemented. To take it a little further I also experimented with the interaction of those drawers. In a previous implementation I went with the press of a button to open and one to close the drawer. As this didn't feel very immersive either I implemented it by having the player drag open or close the drawer by moving the mouse in the desired direction. This more closely resembles how you would open a drawer in real life.

[h2]Vegetation, biomes and improved terrain shading[/h2]
[previewyoutube=Smk5rAHhC-M;full][/previewyoutube]
In order to stay within the target performance and leave more resources for additional content I decided to rework how the vegetation system is managed. The new system is significantly faster even with more diverse and denser vegetation. Due to time constraints I have only implemeted the essential parts of the new system leaving additional work to be done in the future to enable infinite worlds again.
With all the new photorealistic vegetation models the terrain shading no longer matched the quality so I also replaced the terrain shader with a much more modular and powerful one. To properly match the ground textures with the new vegetation I also implemented automatic runtime terrain texturing. Finally I added very basic biome assignment to the world generation pipeline in order to have more varied vegetation throughout the world.


I’m looking forward to reading your thoughts, feedback or criticism in the Steam discussions.

That’s it for this update post. I hope you are all doing well.
Stay safe out there and I’ll see you in the next one.

Norman aka CitrioN

notes.title: Welcome survivors!
notes.notes:
[b]Hello survivors,[/b]

Welcome to the first Steam post for Ozone Wipeout. I would like to use this first post to give you a little bit of insight on the current state of the game, its development and what to look forward to in the future. If you prefer not to read everything in detail you can skip the sections after the TL;DR part.

[h2]TL;DR:[/h2]
[list]
[*]Majority of core systems for the world generation are in place and working well allowing me to switch focus to gameplay and mechanics going forward
[*]With the performance impact of the generation part of the game being lower than expected the change to a photorealistic art style was possible and will be pursued
[*]Gameplay mechanics and art style implementation will be the main focus for the next few months
[*]Monthly news posts on Steam going forward covering the development progress since the previous news
[*]Feel free to follow on any of the social media platforms or join the discord for more in depth and more frequent update posts
[*]Art style changes will be reflected on the steam page as more changes are implemented
[/list]

[h2]Past, Present & Future[/h2]
For about the past 2 years the main focus of the development has been the creation of fundamental systems for the game such as the modding system and most importantly the systems to procedurally generate the world. It has been a massive undertaking with a lot of ups and downs. When I started working on the procedural parts for the game I couldn’t really predict how far I could take the procedural generation because performance is a big factor when it comes to generating content during gameplay. In the beginning of 2022 I successfully finished all the systems with their core functionalities. I’ve created dozens of systems to procedurally generate and populate the entire world with the goal of a fully procedural, authentic looking world for players to enjoy and experience their own unique survival stories in. So far this includes the generation of terrain, road network, building placements, automatic building furnishing, prop placement, item distribution, vegetation and more. With those systems no longer requiring the majority of development time I have started to put more focus on other parts of the game, most importantly the gameplay and mechanics.

[h2]New Art Style: Photorealistic[/h2]
With the core functionalities of the generation in place it was possible to properly test how much performance it actually requires and how much processing power could be allocated for graphics and other parts of the game. Prior to the completion of those essential systems I decided to go with a low poly art style to have graphics using as little processing power as possible in order to allow as much as possible to be used for the generation of the world. After a lot of testing I came to the conclusion that there is enough computational power left to pursue a photorealistic art style on top of the procedural generation. This decision was only made recently so I haven’t had a lot of time yet to replace all of the 3D models in the game. So far I’ve only replaced a small part of the vegetation and a building for demonstration purposes. Over the course of the coming weeks and months all models for items, furniture, buildings etc will be replaced and I’m looking forward to sharing more screenshots and videos with you showcasing those changes and additions in future update posts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41379564/55ddac55715b85092d4cd7c8b74867b7ad85ca05.png[/img]

[h2]Focus for the coming months[/h2]
With the heavy work on procedural systems completed and also other fundamental systems such as the modding system, dynamic save system etc in place the coming months will mostly focus on the addition and implementation of the new photorealistic art style and the creation of various gameplay mechanics. With scavenging being a massive part of the game, the focus for mechanics in the next few months will be centered around that. This for example includes the creation of physical containers which can be pulled open and closed. These physical containers feature actual items inside them instead of a user interface approach used in most games. With the amount of items available in the game I think that this approach will provide the most immersive experience I can deliver by keeping you inside the world and outside of user interfaces for as much as possible.

[h2]General information[/h2]
Starting with this Steam update post I will be posting monthly devlogs here on Steam covering the development progress of one entire month; giving steam followers the opportunity to stay up to date throughout the process of creating the game. I’ve always been very transparent right from the very beginning when I started working on this project in 2019 next to my day job, which in 2021 I decided to pursue full-time. I’ve been posting weekly devlogs for well over 2 years in my discords and will continue to do so. If you are looking for more in-depth and frequent update reports for the game you are very welcome to join the discord or follow on your preferred social media platform(s).

I’m looking forward to reading your thoughts, feedback or criticism in the Steam discussions. So if you have any questions or want to talk about certain aspects related to the game feel free to do so in the discussions and I will try my best to answer them.

That’s it for this first Steam update post. I hope you are all doing well.
Stay safe out there and I’ll see you in the next one.

Norman aka CitrioN
